title: Fewest Edits Between Words
description:
The edit distance between two strings is the minimum number of single-character operations needed to turn the first string into the second. The allowed operations are: insert one character, delete one character, or replace one character with another.

Print the edit distance between the two given strings.

Input format
Line 1: the first string.
Line 2: the second string.

Output format
One integer: the minimum number of operations.
constraints: 1 <= length of each string <= 2000. Both strings contain only lowercase letters a to z.
hints: Think about the two strings one prefix at a time. Let d[i][j] be the edit distance between the first i characters of a and the first j characters of b.
If a[i] equals b[j] no operation is needed for that pair: d[i][j] = d[i-1][j-1]. Otherwise it is 1 plus the smallest of d[i-1][j-1] (replace), d[i-1][j] (delete) and d[i][j-1] (insert).
The base cases are d[i][0] = i and d[0][j] = j. A full table of 2001 x 2001 numbers is fine, or keep only the previous row to save memory.

examples.explanation: kitten -> sitten (replace k) -> sittin (replace e) -> sitting (insert g).
Delete the f, then insert n at the end.
